position: both — *a black car*, *The car is black*
contrast: For people, American newspapers now capitalize *Black*: *Black voters*. Use it as an adjective, never as a noun: *a Black man*, not *a black*, which sounds offensive; *Negro* is outdated and offensive too, so Russian *негр* has no neutral English equivalent. *A black eye* is a bruised eye (синяк под глазом), and *black and blue* means covered in bruises. For humor, *dark* is now more common than *black*: *dark humor*.

senses.gloss: Of the darkest color, like coal or the night sky.
examples: She wore a long *black* dress to the gala.
My car is *black*, so it shows every speck of dust.
Her hair looked even *blacker* under the stage lights.

senses.gloss: Having little or no light; completely dark.
examples: It was pitch *black* in the basement.
The windows were *black* — nobody was home.
The *blackest* skies are in the desert, far from city lights.

senses.gloss: Belonging to a group of people with dark skin, especially of African descent; usually written *Black*.
examples: She was the first *Black* woman elected to the city council.
The museum tells the story of *Black* families in Chicago.

senses.gloss: Of coffee or tea: served without milk or cream.
examples: I take my coffee *black*, no sugar.
A *black* coffee and a blueberry muffin, please.

senses.gloss: Angry, gloomy or without hope; full of bad feeling.
examples: He's been in a *black* mood all morning.
She gave me a *black* look when I mentioned her ex.
After the plant closed, the town's future looked *black*.

senses.gloss: Evil or harmful; connected with the devil.
examples: The villagers believed she practiced *black* magic.
The villain is a man with a *black* heart.

senses.gloss: Of humor or comedy: finding something funny in death, suffering or disaster.
examples: The show is a *black* comedy about a family funeral home.
The play mixes *black* humor with real grief.

position: both — *a white shirt*, *The shirt is white*; *a white lie* only before a noun
contrast: *White hair* is седые волосы, and *go white* means turn pale from shock. *A white lie* is a small, polite lie (невинная ложь), not a serious one. Americans say *coffee with cream* or *coffee with milk*; *white coffee* is British. For people, American style usually writes *white* in lowercase.

senses.gloss: Of the color of snow or milk.
examples: We painted the kitchen *white* to make it look bigger.
He was wearing a *white* T-shirt and jeans.
This toothpaste promises *whiter* teeth in two weeks.

senses.gloss: Belonging to a group of people with light skin, especially of European descent.
examples: Most of the town's residents are *white*.
The survey asked *white* voters and Black voters the same questions.

senses.gloss: Pale in the face from fear, shock or illness.
examples: He went *white* when he saw the bill.
She was *white* as a sheet after the accident.

senses.gloss: Of hair: completely gray from age.
examples: My grandfather's hair turned *white* in his sixties.
A woman with short *white* hair answered the door.

senses.gloss: Of wine, bread or meat: lighter in color than other kinds.
examples: Would you like red or *white* wine with the fish?
Chicken breast is *white* meat.
The kids will only eat *white* bread.

senses.gloss: Harmless and told to be kind or polite, in *a white lie*.
examples: I told a *white* lie and said I loved the sweater.
Everyone tells a *white* lie now and then.

senses.gloss: Of a holiday or season: with snow on the ground.
examples: Denver hasn't had a *white* Christmas in years.
The kids were hoping for a *white* Christmas.

position: both — *a gray sky*, *The sky is gray*
contrast: American spelling is *gray*; *grey* is British, though it survives in names (*Greyhound*, *Earl Grey*). *Gray hair* is седые волосы, not серые, and *go gray* means поседеть. *A gray area* is a situation where the rules are unclear, not a place.

senses.gloss: Of the color between black and white, like ash or rain clouds.
examples: He wore a *gray* suit to the interview.
The paint dried *grayer* than it looked in the can.
Her eyes are *gray*, not blue.

senses.gloss: Of hair: turning white with age; of a person: having such hair.
examples: My dad started going *gray* at forty.
She has a few *gray* hairs and doesn't care.

senses.gloss: Of weather or the sky: cloudy, dull and without sun.
examples: It was a cold, *gray* morning in Seattle.
The sky has been *gray* all week.

senses.gloss: Of the face or skin: pale and unhealthy from illness, tiredness or shock.
examples: He looked *gray* and exhausted after the night shift.
Her face went *gray* when the doctor walked in.

senses.gloss: Dull and without interest or personality.
examples: Life in the suburbs felt *gray* after New York.
The hero is a *gray* little clerk who never takes a risk.

senses.gloss: Not clearly right or wrong, or not clearly defined.
examples: Cash tips are a *gray* area for a lot of workers.
The law is pretty *gray* on this point.

position: both — *brown shoes*, *The shoes are brown*
contrast: *Brown eyes* are карие глаза — English has no separate word. *Brown hair* is каштановые or тёмно-русые волосы; Russian *русые* is usually *light brown* or *dark blond*. *Brown rice* and *brown sugar* are about how the food is processed, not only about the color. About people, *brown* is an adjective, mostly in phrases like *Black and brown communities*; never use it as a noun for a person.

senses.gloss: Of the color of wood, soil or coffee.
examples: He bought a *brown* leather jacket.
The lawn turns *brown* every August.
The leaves get *browner* as fall goes on.

senses.gloss: Of eyes: dark; of hair: any shade from light to dark brown.
examples: The baby has big *brown* eyes.
His hair is light *brown* with a little gray.

senses.gloss: Belonging to a group of people with light to moderately dark skin, especially Latino, Middle Eastern or South Asian; sometimes written *Brown*.
senses.ru: смуглый, темнокожий (о латиноамериканцах, выходцах из Южной Азии и др.)
examples: The program mostly serves Black and *brown* students.
Advocates say *brown* and Black neighborhoods get fewer parks.

senses.gloss: Of skin: darkened by the sun; tanned.
examples: The kids came back from camp *brown* from the sun.
By August he was as *brown* as a lifeguard.

senses.gloss: Of rice, bread or sugar: not fully refined, keeping more of the grain or the dark syrup.
senses.ru: бурый (о рисе), из муки грубого помола; коричневый (о сахаре)
examples: I'll have the chicken with *brown* rice.
Add a cup of packed *brown* sugar.

position: both — *a pink dress*, *The dress is pink*
contrast: *Tickled pink* means very pleased, not ticklish. *A pink slip* (a noun) is a notice that you have lost your job. For a face red from embarrassment, *pink* is milder than *red*: *She went pink* is a light blush.

senses.gloss: Of a pale red color.
examples: She painted her nails bright *pink*.
My daughter wanted a *pink* bike for her birthday.
The sky got *pinker* as the sun went down.

senses.gloss: Of the face or skin: slightly red from health, heat or embarrassment.
examples: His cheeks went *pink* when she thanked him.
The baby's skin was soft and *pink*.

position: both — *a purple scarf*, *The scarf is purple*; *purple prose* only before a noun
contrast: False friend: Russian *пурпурный* leans toward crimson, while *purple* is фиолетовый or лиловый — the color of eggplant and grape juice. *Violet* is a bluer purple; *lavender* and *lilac* are pale purples. In US politics *red* is Republican and *blue* is Democratic, so a *purple* state is split between them.

senses.gloss: Of a color between red and blue.
examples: The grapes were dark *purple* and very sweet.
She dyed her hair *purple* for the concert.
The bruise turned *more purple* overnight.

senses.gloss: Of the face or skin: dark red from anger, cold or effort.
examples: He turned *purple* with rage.
Her hands were *purple* from the cold.

senses.gloss: Of writing: too elaborate, full of fancy words and emotion.
examples: The novel is full of *purple* prose about sunsets.
Cut the *purple* passages and get to the point.

senses.gloss: Of a US state or area: with about equal support for Republicans and Democrats.
examples: Colorado used to be a *purple* state.
The suburbs around Atlanta are turning *purple*.

position: both — *an orange vest*, *The vest is orange*
contrast: Red human hair is *red* in English, not *orange*: a рыжий человек is *a redhead*. For animals, *orange* is normal: *an orange cat*. In *orange juice* the modifier is the noun *orange* (the fruit), not the color adjective.

senses.gloss: Of a color between red and yellow.
examples: Hunters wear *orange* vests in the woods.
The maple leaves turn *orange* in October.
The sunset got *more orange* as we watched.

senses.gloss: Of an animal's fur: reddish yellow.
examples: We adopted an *orange* tabby from the shelter.
Our dog is white with *orange* patches on her back.

position: both — *a yellow bus*, *The bus is yellow*
contrast: Russian *жёлтая пресса* is *the tabloids* or *tabloid journalism* in modern American English; *yellow journalism* is mainly a historical term for the 1890s newspaper wars. *Yellow* meaning cowardly is informal and old-fashioned. The middle traffic light is *yellow* in American English (*run a yellow light*); *amber* is British. Never use *yellow* to describe people of East Asian descent: it is a racial slur.

senses.gloss: Of the color of lemons or butter.
examples: The kids ran out to the *yellow* school bus.
Our house is *yellow* with white trim.
The old photos have gotten *yellower* with age.

senses.gloss: Cowardly — informal and old-fashioned.
examples: He was too *yellow* to stand up to his boss.
Don't be *yellow* — just go talk to her.

senses.gloss: Of news reporting: shocking and exaggerated to sell papers, in *yellow journalism*.
examples: Hearst's papers were famous for *yellow* journalism.
Critics called the cable coverage a new kind of *yellow* journalism.

position: both — *green eyes*, *Her eyes are green*
takes: *with envy* — only in the 'jealous' sense: *green with envy*
contrast: *Green* for 'inexperienced' matches Russian *зелёный*. Envy is *green with envy*, not *green from envy*. *Green* in *green energy* or *go green* means good for the environment, not the color. *A green card* is the US permanent resident card, and *greens* (a noun) are leafy vegetables.

senses.gloss: Of the color of grass and leaves.
examples: She has bright *green* eyes.
Wait until the light turns *green*.
The grass is always *greener* on the other side.

senses.gloss: Covered with grass, trees or other plants.
examples: Portland has a lot of *green* space for a big city.
The hills are *green* after the spring rains.

senses.gloss: Of fruit: not yet ripe.
examples: These bananas are still *green*.
Don't pick the tomatoes while they're *green*.

senses.gloss: Young and without experience.
examples: The new hires are pretty *green*, so be patient with them.
I was *green* when I started, and I made every mistake.

senses.gloss: Good for the environment, or supporting its protection.
examples: The company is trying to go *green*.
*Green* energy now powers half the city.
Stores are switching to *greener* packaging.

senses.gloss: Pale and sick-looking, as if about to vomit.
examples: He looked a little *green* after the roller coaster.
She turned *green* as soon as the boat left the dock.

senses.gloss: Very jealous, in *green with envy*.
examples: My friends were *green* with envy when they saw my new car.
His success left the other writers *green* with envy.

senses.gloss: Of wood: freshly cut and not yet dried.
examples: *Green* wood smokes a lot when you burn it.
Don't build the deck with *green* lumber.

position: both — *blue eyes*, *Her eyes are blue*; 'sad' mostly after a verb: *feeling blue*
contrast: English has one basic word, *blue*, for both синий and голубой: say *light blue* for голубой and *dark blue* or *navy* for тёмно-синий. Russian slang *голубой* ('gay') does not carry over — *blue* never means gay. In US politics *blue* is Democratic and *red* is Republican, the reverse of most European party colors. Spelling: *bluer*, *bluest*, with no extra *e*.

senses.gloss: Of the color of a clear sky or the sea.
examples: She has bright *blue* eyes.
The sky was *blue* all weekend.
The water gets *bluer* the farther out you go.

senses.gloss: Sad or depressed — informal.
examples: I've been feeling kind of *blue* since the holidays.
Rainy Sundays always make me *blue*.

senses.gloss: In US politics: voting for or controlled by Democrats.
examples: California is a solidly *blue* state.
The district turned *blue* in the last election.

senses.gloss: Of the skin or lips: bluish from cold or lack of air.
examples: The kids' lips were *blue* after swimming in the lake.
His fingers were *blue* with cold.

senses.gloss: Of jokes or language: rude, especially about sex.
examples: The comedian's act was a little too *blue* for TV.
He told some *blue* jokes at the bachelor party.

position: both — *a beige sofa*, *The sofa is beige*
contrast: The word ends in the soft *zh* sound of *garage*, not the *j* sound of *badge*. Americans also say *tan* for a darker beige and *khaki* for the light brownish color of casual pants. *Beige* meaning 'boring' is informal.

senses.gloss: Of a pale sandy brown color.
examples: We picked a *beige* sofa that goes with everything.
The walls in the rental are all *beige*.
The new carpet is even *more beige* than the old one.

senses.gloss: Boring and without character — informal.
examples: The hotel was clean but completely *beige*.
Their music is pleasant but a little *beige*.

position: both — *a navy blazer*, *The blazer is navy*
contrast: *Navy* alone as a color means *navy blue*. Before nouns like *officer* or *base*, *Navy* is the noun (*a Navy officer*); the adjective for 'relating to a navy' is *naval* (военно-морской): *a naval base*.

senses.gloss: Of a very dark blue color.
examples: He wore a *navy* blazer with khakis.
The team's uniforms are *navy* with gold numbers.
She painted the front door *navy*.

position: both — *a maroon sweater*, *The sweater is maroon*
contrast: Russian *бордовый* is usually *maroon* (browner) or *burgundy* (more purple-red). Do not confuse the color with the verb *maroon*: *marooned on an island* means left stranded there.

senses.gloss: Of a dark brownish-red color.
examples: The school colors are *maroon* and white.
He showed up in a *maroon* sweater.
Her new car is *maroon*, not red.

position: both — *turquoise water*, *The water is turquoise*
contrast: The stress is on the first syllable: TUR-kwoyz. *Turquoise* is also the noun for the stone, so *a turquoise ring* can mean a ring set with turquoise, not only a ring of that color.

senses.gloss: Of a bright greenish-blue color.
examples: We snorkeled in the *turquoise* water off Key West.
The tiles in her kitchen are *turquoise*.
The lake looked *more turquoise* in the afternoon sun.

position: both — the color and *you're golden* after a verb; *a golden opportunity*, *golden age*, *golden anniversary* only before a noun
contrast: *Gold* (the noun) is the usual word for things made of gold: *a gold ring*, *gold earrings*. *Golden* is mostly the color (*golden hair*, *golden brown*) and the figurative senses (*a golden opportunity*); *a golden ring* sounds like a fairy tale. *You're golden* is informal American English for 'you're all set'.

senses.gloss: Having the color of gold; shiny yellow.
examples: Bake the pie until the crust is *golden* brown.
She has long *golden* hair.
The fields looked *more golden* in the evening light.

senses.gloss: Made of gold — literary or old-fashioned.
examples: The king wore a *golden* crown.
In the story, the goose lays *golden* eggs.

senses.gloss: Of a period: very happy, successful or prosperous.
examples: The 1930s and '40s were the *golden* age of Hollywood.
They spent their *golden* years traveling the country.

senses.gloss: Very good and likely to bring success, of a chance or opportunity.
examples: This is a *golden* opportunity to meet investors.
He missed a *golden* chance to tie the game.

senses.gloss: Admired by everyone and expected to succeed, in *golden boy* and *golden girl*.
examples: He was the *golden* boy of Silicon Valley.
In high school she was the *golden* girl who could do no wrong.

senses.gloss: Of an anniversary: the fiftieth.
examples: My parents celebrated their *golden* anniversary in June.
A *golden* anniversary calls for a big party.

senses.gloss: In a good position, with nothing to worry about — informal, after a verb.
examples: Get a B on the final and you're *golden*.
Once the paperwork is signed, we're *golden*.

position: both — *a silver car*, *The car is silver*; the anniversary sense only before a noun
comparison: not gradable — *silvery* is the word for 'somewhat silver'
contrast: *A silver ring* (серебряное кольцо) uses the noun *silver* for the material, like *a gold ring*, so 'made of silver' is not a sense here. The adjective is the color: *a silver car* is серебристая машина. *Silvery* means 'somewhat silver' and also describes a soft, clear sound: *a silvery voice*. *Silver hair* is a flattering way to say gray hair.

senses.gloss: Having the shiny gray color of silver.
examples: She drives a *silver* Honda.
Her dress was *silver* and covered in sequins.
The *silver* balloons matched the tablecloths.

senses.gloss: Of hair: gray or white in a shiny, attractive way.
examples: The anchor was a handsome man with *silver* hair.
Her hair went *silver* in her fifties, and she loved it.

senses.gloss: Of an anniversary: the twenty-fifth.
examples: They threw a party for their *silver* anniversary.
The theater celebrates its *silver* jubilee this year.

position: both — *blond hair*, *His hair is blond*
contrast: American style usually writes *blond* for the adjective, whoever it describes; *blonde* is also common, especially about women and for the noun *a blonde*. *Blond hair* is светлые волосы; Russian *русые* is usually *light brown* or *dark blond*. *Fair* also means light hair or skin and sounds more literary.

senses.gloss: Of hair: pale yellow or light in color.
examples: Her hair is naturally *blond*.
He has short *blond* hair and a beard.
My hair gets *blonder* every summer.

senses.gloss: Of a person: having light-colored hair.
examples: Their son is *blond* like his mother.
A tall *blond* guy in a red jacket was waiting outside.

senses.gloss: Of wood, beer and some other things: light in color.
examples: The table is made of *blond* oak.
The brewery's *blond* ale is light and crisp.

position: both — *a pale face*, *You look pale*; *a pale imitation* only before a noun
contrast: *Pale* skin often suggests illness or too little sun; *fair* skin is neutral or flattering. Before a color word, *pale* means light: *pale blue*, *pale pink*. Spelling: *paler*, *palest*, adding only *-r* and *-st*. *Beyond the pale* (unacceptable) uses an old noun, not this adjective.

senses.gloss: Of the face or skin: having less color than usual, from illness, shock or little sun.
examples: You look *pale* — are you OK?
She's naturally *pale* and burns easily.
He looked even *paler* after the second round of tests.

senses.gloss: Of a color: light, with a lot of white in it.
examples: He wore a *pale* blue shirt and a dark tie.
We chose the *palest* shade of yellow for the nursery.

senses.gloss: Of light: weak and not bright.
examples: We left in the *pale* light of early morning.
A *pale* moon hung over the lake.

senses.gloss: Weaker or worse than the original, in *a pale imitation* or *a pale shadow*.
examples: The sequel is a *pale* imitation of the first movie.
The team is a *pale* shadow of what it was ten years ago.

position: both — *a dark room*, *The room is dark*
contrast: Russian *темно* is *It's dark*, with the adjective, not *It's darkly*. *Dark chocolate* is горький шоколад, and *dark meat* is the meat of chicken legs and thighs. *Dark skin* is тёмная or смуглая кожа. Russian *тёмная личность* is *a shady character*, not *a dark person*. *In the dark* (не в курсе) is a noun phrase.

senses.gloss: With little or no light.
examples: It gets *dark* around five in December.
The hallway was *dark* and quiet.
The sky got *darker* as the storm rolled in.

senses.gloss: Of a color: deep and closer to black.
examples: He wore a *dark* blue suit to the funeral.
Her car is *dark* green.

senses.gloss: Of hair, eyes or skin: brown or black.
examples: He has *dark* hair and *dark* eyes.
She's tall, with *dark* skin and short hair.

senses.gloss: Sad, frightening or unpleasant; without hope.
examples: Those were *dark* days for the company.
The movie takes a *dark* turn halfway through.
The book's humor is *darker* than I expected.

senses.gloss: Evil or threatening.
examples: The novel explores the *darkest* parts of human nature.
There's a *dark* side to his charm.

senses.gloss: Of a theater, TV station or website: closed or not operating.
examples: Most Broadway theaters are *dark* on Mondays.
The station went *dark* after it lost its license.

senses.gloss: Of food or drink: darker than others of its kind and usually stronger in flavor.
examples: *Dark* chocolate has less sugar than milk chocolate.
Do you want white meat or *dark* meat?
She likes a *dark* roast in the morning.

position: both — *a light bag*, *The bag is light*; *light on* only after a verb
takes: *on* + noun — having too little of something: *light on details*
contrast: *Light* covers two unrelated ideas: 'not heavy' (лёгкий) and 'not dark' (светлый). But Russian *лёгкий* meaning 'not difficult' is *easy*: *an easy test*, not *a light test*. *A light sleeper* wakes easily (чутко спит). *Lite* is a spelling used on food labels (*lite beer*). *Light on your feet* means moving easily and gracefully, not 'lacking' like *light on details*. *Travel light* and *sleep light* use the adverb, and *a lighter* is a noun (зажигалка).

senses.gloss: Not heavy; weighing little.
examples: This laptop is really *light*.
Aluminum bikes are *lighter* than steel ones.
Bring a *light* jacket for the evening.

senses.gloss: Of a color: pale, not deep.
examples: She has *light* brown hair.
Choose a *lighter* shade of paint for a small room.

senses.gloss: Full of natural light; not dark.
examples: In June it's still *light* outside at nine.
The apartment is big and *light*.

senses.gloss: Small in amount, force or number.
examples: A *light* rain fell all afternoon.
Traffic is *light* on Sunday mornings.

senses.gloss: Not needing much physical effort.
examples: After surgery, he was on *light* duty for a month.
Do some *light* stretching before you run.

senses.gloss: Not serious; meant to entertain.
examples: I want some *light* reading for the beach.
The conversation stayed *light* and friendly.

senses.gloss: Of food or drink: small, easy to digest, or low in fat, calories or alcohol.
examples: We had a *light* lunch of soup and salad.
Can I get a *light* beer?

senses.gloss: Gentle, with little pressure.
examples: She felt a *light* touch on her shoulder.
We heard *light* footsteps on the stairs.

senses.gloss: Of sleep: easily broken; of a sleeper: waking easily.
examples: I'm a *light* sleeper, so the dog wakes me up.
He fell into a *light* sleep on the couch.

senses.gloss: Having too little of something — in *light on*.
examples: The report is *light* on details.
The menu is a little *light* on vegetarian options.

position: both — *a bright light*, *The light is bright*
contrast: *A bright person* is smart (умный, способный), not яркий: Russian *яркая личность* is *a colorful personality* or *a striking person*. *A bright idea* is often sarcastic. After verbs like *shine*, careful writing uses the adverb *brightly*, although *shine bright* is common in songs and speech.

senses.gloss: Giving out or full of strong light.
examples: The *bright* lights of Las Vegas never go off.
The kitchen is *bright* and sunny.
The new phone's screen is much *brighter* than my old one.

senses.gloss: Of a color: strong and vivid.
examples: He bought a *bright* red pickup.
She always wears *bright* colors.

senses.gloss: Of weather or a day: sunny and clear.
examples: It was a *bright*, cold morning.
The day was *bright* but windy.

senses.gloss: Intelligent and quick to learn.
examples: She's one of the *brightest* kids in her class.
He's a *bright* guy, but he never studies.

senses.gloss: Of an idea: clever — often used sarcastically.
examples: Whose *bright* idea was it to drive in this snow?
Then I had a *bright* idea: call the landlord.

senses.gloss: Cheerful and lively.
examples: She greeted us with a *bright* smile.
His voice sounded *bright* and happy on the phone.

senses.gloss: Likely to be successful or good.
examples: You have a *bright* future ahead of you.
The outlook for the economy isn't very *bright*.

position: both — *a round table*, *The table is round*
contrast: Russian *круглый* in set phrases is not *round*: *круглый год* is *all year round* (an adverb), *круглые сутки* is *around the clock*, *круглый отличник* is *a straight-A student*. *A round-trip ticket* (туда и обратно) is a compound adjective. *Round* as a preposition (*round the corner*) is British; Americans say *around*. *A round* (noun) is a раунд or a round of drinks.

senses.gloss: Shaped like a circle or a ball.
examples: We sat at a big *round* table.
The earth is *round*, not flat.
This pumpkin is *rounder* than the other one.

senses.gloss: Of a face or body: full and curved.
examples: The baby has a *round* face and big eyes.
She has *round* cheeks and a big smile.

senses.gloss: Of a number: whole, not exact, usually ending in zero.
examples: Just give me a *round* number — I don't need it to the penny.
In *round* numbers, the project will cost a million.

senses.gloss: Of a sound or flavor: full and smooth.
examples: The wine has a *round*, soft finish.
She has a warm, *round* singing voice.

position: both — *a square box*, *The box is square*; after a measurement for each side: *ten feet square*
contrast: Word order changes the meaning: *100 square feet* is an area, but *a room ten feet square* measures ten feet on each side (100 square feet in all). *Square* also means 'even, owing nothing' (*We're square* = мы в расчёте). *A square* (noun) is a площадь in a city: *Times Square*. *More square* is as common as *squarer*.

senses.gloss: Having four equal sides and four right angles.
examples: Cut the dough into *square* pieces.
The napkins are *square*, not round.
Her new glasses have *more square* frames than her old ones.

senses.gloss: Of a jaw or shoulders: broad and solid, with strong angles.
examples: The actor has a strong, *square* jaw.
He stood with his shoulders *square* and his head up.

senses.gloss: Used in measurements of area (*square feet*), or after a length to give each side of a square.
senses.ru: квадратный (о мере площади); со стороной (о размере)
examples: The apartment is 800 *square* feet.
The rug is six feet *square*.

senses.gloss: Fair and honest.
examples: The dealer gave us a *square* deal.
I've always been *square* with you.

senses.gloss: Even: owing nothing, or having the same score.
senses.ru: в расчёте, квиты; с равным счётом
examples: You paid for lunch, so now we're *square*.
The match was all *square* after nine holes.

senses.gloss: Of a meal: full and satisfying.
examples: The shelter serves three *square* meals a day.
When did you last eat a *square* meal?

senses.gloss: Old-fashioned and boring — dated slang.
examples: My parents were so *square* in the '80s.
Don't be *square* — come to the party.

position: both — *an oval mirror*, *The mirror is oval*
contrast: *Oval* is both the adjective (овальный) and the noun (овал), so no ending changes: *an oval table*, *shaped like an oval*. *The Oval Office* is the president's office in the White House.

senses.gloss: Shaped like an egg or a stretched circle.
examples: An *oval* mirror hung over the sink.
The track around the field is *oval*.
Her face is *more oval* than round.

position: both — *a triangular sign*, *The sign is triangular*; the 'three parties' sense only before a noun
contrast: *Triangular* sounds a little formal; in casual speech Americans often say *triangle-shaped* or use the noun: *Cut it into triangles*. *A triangular relationship* is what everyday English calls *a love triangle* (любовный треугольник).

senses.gloss: Shaped like a triangle.
examples: Yield signs in the US are *triangular*.
Cut the sandwiches into *triangular* pieces.
The park sits on a small *triangular* lot.

senses.gloss: Involving three people, groups or places.
examples: The novel is about a *triangular* relationship between two sisters and one man.
*Triangular* trade linked Europe, Africa and the Americas.

position: both — *a rectangular table*, *The table is rectangular*
contrast: False friend: *rectangular* describes only four-sided shapes. Russian *прямоугольный треугольник* is *a right triangle* in American English (*right-angled triangle* in British), and *прямой угол* is *a right angle*.

senses.gloss: Shaped like a rectangle: four straight sides and four right angles, usually with two sides longer.
examples: We need a *rectangular* table that seats eight.
The pool in the backyard is *rectangular*.
Most phone screens are *rectangular* with rounded corners.

position: both — *a circular window*, *The window is circular*
contrast: In everyday speech Americans say *round* for most objects (*a round table*); *circular* sounds more formal or technical and suits flat shapes, routes and movement. *Circular reasoning* is рассуждение по кругу. *A circular* (noun) is a printed ad or flyer.

senses.gloss: Shaped like a circle.
examples: The church has a large *circular* window over the door.
The main room of the museum is *circular*.

senses.gloss: Moving in a circle, or ending where it began.
examples: There's a *circular* trail around the lake.
Rub the cream in with small *circular* motions.

senses.gloss: Of an argument: using what it wants to prove as its proof.
examples: That's *circular* reasoning, and it won't convince anyone.
Her argument is *circular*: the book is true because the book says so.

position: both — *a curved blade*, *The blade is curved*
contrast: *Curved* means bending smoothly (изогнутый). Russian *кривой* in the sense 'not straight as it should be' is *crooked*: *a crooked picture*, *crooked teeth*. *Curvy* means having many curves, like a mountain road, or describes a full, shapely figure.

senses.gloss: Bent in a smooth line, not straight.
examples: The chef uses a knife with a *curved* blade.
The front of the building is *curved* like a wave.
This year's gaming monitors are *more curved* than last year's.

position: both — *a wooden spoon*, *The floors are wooden*
comparison: more/most — only in the 'stiff' sense: *more wooden*, *most wooden*
contrast: For the material, Americans use the noun as often as the adjective: *wood floors* and *a wood table* are as common as *wooden floors*. Only *wooden* has the figurative sense 'stiff, without expression': *wooden acting*, never *wood acting*.

senses.gloss: Made of wood.
examples: We crossed an old *wooden* bridge over the creek.
Stir the sauce with a *wooden* spoon.
All the floors in the house are *wooden*.

senses.gloss: Stiff and awkward, without natural feeling or expression.
examples: The lead actor's performance was *wooden*.
His second speech was even *more wooden* than the first.

position: both — mostly before a noun; after a verb the noun is more natural: *The scarf is wool*
contrast: American spelling has one *l*: *woolen*; *woollen* is British. In everyday speech the noun is more common: *a wool sweater*, *The scarf is 100% wool*. The noun *woolens* means wool clothes.

senses.gloss: Made of wool.
examples: Pack *woolen* socks for the camping trip.
She knitted a *woolen* hat for the baby.
Everything she wore that winter was *woolen*, from her hat to her socks.

senses.gloss: Relating to making or selling wool cloth.
examples: The town grew up around a *woolen* mill.
New England's *woolen* industry declined in the twentieth century.

position: both — *a plastic smile*, *Everything there felt plastic*; *plastic surgery* only before a noun
comparison: more/most — in the 'fake' sense: *more plastic*, *most plastic*
contrast: *A plastic bag* and *plastic cups* (пластиковые) use the noun *plastic* as a modifier, like *a glass door*, so 'made of plastic' is not a sense here. False friend: Russian *пластичный* about a dancer is *graceful* or *fluid*, not *plastic*; *plastic* about a person means fake. *Plastic* (a noun, informal) also means credit cards: *Do you take plastic?*

senses.gloss: Relating to shaping or repairing forms, in *plastic surgery* and *plastic arts*.
examples: She's a *plastic* surgeon in Miami.
He needed *plastic* surgery on his face after the accident.
Sculpture and ceramics are *plastic* arts.

senses.gloss: Artificial and insincere; fake.
examples: The flight attendant gave us a *plastic* smile.
The whole resort felt fake and *plastic*.
The remake looks even *more plastic* than the original.

senses.gloss: Easily shaped or changed.
examples: Wet clay is *plastic* and easy to mold.
A young child's brain is highly *plastic*.

position: both — *metallic paint*, *The paint is metallic*
contrast: For everyday objects made of metal, use the noun: *a metal door*, *a metal box* (металлическая дверь, коробка). *Metallic* usually describes how something looks, sounds or tastes: *metallic paint*, *a metallic taste*, or is a science word: *metallic elements*.

senses.gloss: Shiny, like metal.
examples: The car comes in *metallic* gray.
She wore a *metallic* gold dress to the party.
The fabric looks *more metallic* under bright lights.

senses.gloss: Tasting or sounding like metal.
examples: The tap water has a *metallic* taste.
We heard a loud *metallic* clang from the garage.

senses.gloss: Containing metal, or having the properties of a metal.
examples: Airport scanners detect *metallic* objects.
Sodium is a soft, *metallic* element.
